    \texttt{aged\_battery} & unseen & Worn battery pack - only 12 Wh left (55 \% of new) and a slower 15 W charger, so charging has to be planned carefully.\\[2pt]
    \texttt{balanced} & seen & Nominal rates A=20, B=30, C=5 units/h, rare faults, healthy fully charged robot.\\[2pt]
    \texttt{fault\_burst} & seen & Worn machines (health 60 \%) failing about once per hour with 15 min repairs - lines stop and restart unpredictably.\\[2pt]
    \texttt{heavy\_load} & unseen & Worst realistic day - double production, heavier parts and a half-charged robot. Slightly beyond what one robot can keep up with (utilisation ~1.03), so some loss is unavoidable - the question is how little.\\[2pt]
    \texttt{heavy\_parts} & unseen & Heavy product mix - units weigh about twice as much, so fewer fit per trip and every trip costs more energy.\\[2pt]
    \texttt{high\_demand} & seen & All lines at 2x the nominal rate (A=40, B=60, C=10 units/h) - robot utilisation ~0.85, near its capacity.\\[2pt]
    \texttt{hot\_factory} & unseen & Summer - 38 C in the hall and poor cooling, so the motors run hot and long heavy trips risk the temperature limit.\\[2pt]
    \texttt{low\_battery\_start} & seen & Robot starts with 30 \% battery while the buffers are already half full.\\[2pt]
    \texttt{one\_hot\_section} & seen & Section B runs at double speed (60 units/h, one unit per minute) and blocks within 10 min if neglected.\\[2pt]
    \texttt{section\_breakdown} & unseen & Section B's machine is failing - health 35 \%, frequent faults and long repairs - while A and C run normally.\\[2pt]
    \texttt{small\_buffers} & unseen & Lean production - output buffers hold only a few units, so lines block within minutes unless served on time.\\[2pt]
    \texttt{worn\_robot} & seen & Robot drive condition 45 \% (draws more energy, close to the maintenance limit) in the nominal factory.\\[2pt]
